A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, and their complete main texts, displays, and supplementary material support comparison. PCLDA in v1 matches lda◦pca in v2; relocated tables and multiclass theorems can also be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original Monte Carlo simulations, classification results for leukaemia and lung cancer data, and supplementary feature-selection analyses. Section 2.2 also reports a replicated whitening demonstration.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations, cancer-data classification results, and supplementary numerical analyses in Sections 4 and 7.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 and Algorithm 4 introduce qda◦pca with separate class-specific whitening matrices, selection of whitened-mean supports, a quadratic score, and a threshold minimizing training classification error. The existing binary and multiclass PCLDA procedures are otherwise retained under the lda◦pca name.

E1.justification: v1's bivariate Gaussian demonstration in the low-dimensional, nonsingular-covariance regime is removed. The three high-dimensional simulation models and both cancer datasets remain. The unequal-covariance extension is theoretical and does not add evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Deleting v1's Example 1 removes its comparisons against raw-coordinate thresholding and full plug-in LDA. The main experiments retain NSC, SLDA, DSDA, AdaLDA, CAT-LDA, and the corresponding rotated or regularized variants. Newly discussed related methods are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The removed demonstration used 500 observations per class and in-sample error, false-positive, and false-negative rates. Retained experiments preserve their sample sizes, data splits, preprocessing, cross-validation procedures, and tuning settings; no new empirical QDA protocol is reported.

E4.justification: v1's Example 1, Figures 1–2, and Table 1 examine how thresholding raw versus whitened coordinates affects classification; this analysis is removed. Strong-versus-weak feature-selection analyses and covariance condition-number diagnostics remain in v2's supplementary material.

E5.justification: The reporting of 1,000 replications for v1's whitening demonstration disappears with that experiment. Retained simulations still use 200 Monte Carlo replications and report standard deviations. Adding the existing replication count to table captions does not establish additional runs or a new uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: v1's Table 1 results are removed, including error rates of 30.88%, 16.55%, and 12.56% for raw-coordinate thresholding, whitened-coordinate thresholding, and full plug-in LDA. Numerical values in the retained experimental and supplementary tables match after renaming and relocation; no QDA results are added.

T1.justification: v2 strengthens the main spike-growth assumption from O(p) to Θ(p), corrects mathematical expressions, revises perturbation derivations, and changes several stated failure probabilities from O(p^-1) to O(p^-2). It adds optimization formulations, an eigenvalue-ratio argument, and QDA assumptions with Theorem 6 and its proof. Existing multiclass Theorems 4–5 move to Section 8.5 with revised assumptions.

C1.justification: The introduction and Remark 3 broaden the claimed contributions to Bayes consistency for PCA combined with QDA under unequal class covariances. v2 also recasts the work as analysis of a prototypical lda◦pca classifier rather than proposing PCLDA. The competitive-error and reduced-feature-count claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of why sparse whitened directions can accommodate dense original discriminant directions, why non-leading principal components can matter, and why estimating the whitening transformation differs from specifying a fixed generalized-Lasso penalty. Interpretations of the retained experiments and most covariance-structure limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds guidance for selecting the unknown spike count, including factor-selection references and an explicit eigenvalue-ratio construction after Theorem 1. The documented benchmark tuning choices and software-access links remain unchanged; this additional guidance does not establish changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 and Remark 3 substantially expand positioning relative to generalized Lasso, the principal-component classifiers of Bing and colleagues, and Sifaou et al.'s spiked-covariance classifiers. Section 5.3 additionally relates the extension to sparse QDA and common-principal-component methods, going beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Exposition and proofs undergo extensive editing, PCLDA is renamed throughout, and related work receives a dedicated section with subsections. The worked whitening example is deleted, extension sections are reorganized, and multiclass theoretical statements move into the restructured supplementary material.

P2.justification: v2 substantially changes typography, text width, spacing, and table placement. Both original figures and their demonstration table disappear, the strong/weak-signal table moves to the supplement, the existing rotation procedure becomes an algorithm display, and a new QDA algorithm display is added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the precision of the main spike-growth assumptions and provides more informative research positioning. However, its new Eq. (5.9) discards quadratic contributions outside the whitened-mean supports without assumptions ensuring their cancellation, leaving a material gap in the argument supporting Theorem 6's Bayes-consistency claim. These gains and the unresolved validity of a substantial new contribution prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
